# PCAdapt

```{r}
# install and load pcadapt
#install.packages("pcadapt")
library(pcadapt)
```

## Original File `SNP.TRSBOTHdp5g5mafMIp9g9dnDNAmaf052A.recode.vcf`

```{r}
# Convert VCF file to pcadapt format
vcf2pcadapt("SNP.TRSBOTHdp5g5mafMIp9g9dnDNAmaf052A.recode.vcf", output = "tmp.pcadapt", allele.sep = c("/", "|"))

pcadapt_file <- read.pcadapt("tmp.pcadapt", type = "pcadapt")
```

```{r}
# Choosing the number K of Principal Components
# We start off with a large number of PCs
x <- pcadapt(input = pcadapt_file, K = 20)
```

```{r}
# Plot the likelihoods using a screeplot
plot(x, option = "screeplot")
```

```{r}
# Plotting likelihoods again, but with 10 Principal Components
plot(x, option = "screeplot", K = 10)
```

```{r}
# Create population designations 
poplist.names <- c(rep("BAR", 10),rep("BIS", 10),rep("GB", 10),rep("GHP", 10), rep("KIC", 10),rep("MCD", 10),rep("NAR", 10), rep("NAR2", 10), rep("PVD", 10))
```

```{r}
# Create a score plot 
#Plot the first two PCs
plot(x, option = "scores", pop = poplist.names)
```

```{r}
x$singular.values
```



## NAR2 removed File `SNP.TRSBOTHdp5g5mafMIp9g9dnDNAmaf052A8.recode.vcf`

```{r}
# Convert VCF file to pcadapt format
```

In PCs one and two, there are two regions of known inversions - likely due to remixing of genetic material across ocean basins through non-wild oysters. 

Before performing LD thinning, I want to explore the SNPs that fall around the 25,000 index marker. Looking at the Manhattan plot, we can see SNPs with low p-values between indices 30,000 and 40,000. These correspond to inversions on chromosomes 5 and 6. However, there is another cluster of SNPs with low p-values around index 25,000. I want to check the chromosome and position of these SNPs to see if they are tied to another structural variant. 

```{r}
qval8_notthin <- qvalue(x1$pvalues)$qvalues
alpha8 <- 0.1 # expected false discovery rate lower than 1% - raised from 0.05
```

#### Save Outliers

```{r}
outliers8_notthin <- which(qval8_notthin < alpha8)
outliers8_notthin
```

```{r}
# Save outliers to .txt file 
invisible(lapply(outliers8_notthin, write, "outliers8_pcadapt_notthinned.txt", append=TRUE))
```

In terminal:

Taking the SNP indices and applying chromosome and position info:

```
$ cat  outliers8_pcadapt_notthinned.txt | parallel "grep -w ^{} loci1.plus.index" | cut -f2,3> outlier8_pcadapt_notthinned.loci.txt
```

Based on the list of outliers above, SNPs around index 25,000 are approximately in rows 961-1200. I can search for these rows in the loci txt file to identify their chromosome and position.

```
$ sed -n '961,1200p' outlier_pcadapt_notthinned.loci.txt
```

This will print out all the info in these rows. Here's a glimpse: 

```
NC_035783.1	42344300
NC_035783.1	42344330
NC_035783.1	42344351
NC_035783.1	42344364
NC_035783.1	42344377
NC_035783.1	42344429
NC_035783.1	42344916
```

The SNPs around index 25,000 fall on chromosome 4. 


Back in R for LD thinning.


```{r}
# performing SNP thinning in order to compute PCs
res <- pcadapt(filename, K = 20, LD.clumping = list(size = 5000, thr = 0.05))
plot(res, option = "screeplot")
```
```{r}
res <- pcadapt(filename, K = 2, LD.clumping = list(size = 5000, thr = 0.05))
par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
for (i in 1:2)
  plot(res$loadings[, i], pch = 19, cex = .3, ylab = paste0("Loadings PC", i))
```

```{r}
plot(res)
```

#### Assigning an alpha value

```{r}
library(qvalue) # transforms p-values into q-values.
```

```{r}
qval1 <- qvalue(res$pvalues)$qvalues
alpha <- 0.1 # expected false discovery rate lower than 10%
```

#### Save Outliers

```{r}
outliers <- which(qval1 < alpha)
outliers
```

```{r}
# Save outliers to .txt file 
invisible(lapply(outliers, write, "outliers_pcadapt_thinned_8pops.txt", append=TRUE))
```


# OutFLANK

```{r}
# Load all necessary packages
library(OutFLANK)  # outflank package
library(vcfR)
library(bigsnpr)   # package for Linkage Disequilibrium pruning
```

```{r}
# Convert VCF to OutFLANK format
my_vcf <- read.vcfR("SNP.TRSBOTHdp5g5mafMIp9g9dnDNAmaf052A8.recode.vcf")

geno <- extract.gt(my_vcf) # Character matrix containing the genotypes
position <- getPOS(my_vcf) # Positions in bp
chromosome <- getCHROM(my_vcf) # Chromosome information

G <- matrix(NA, nrow = nrow(geno), ncol = ncol(geno))

G[geno %in% c("0/0", "0|0")] <- 0
G[geno  %in% c("0/1", "1/0", "1|0", "0|1")] <- 1
G[geno %in% c("1/1", "1|1")] <- 2

# NA should be replaced with “9” to work with the functions in the OutFLANK package
G[is.na(G)] <- 9

head(G[,1:10])
```

```{r}
# Convert pop designations to a vector
pop <- as.vector(poplist.names1)
pop
```

```{r}
# Calculate Fst
my_fst <- MakeDiploidFSTMat(t(G), locusNames = paste0(chromosome,"_", position), popNames = pop)

head(my_fst)
# the output will be a table showing Fst statistics for each locus
```

```{r}
# Plot heterozygosity vs Fst
plot(my_fst$He, my_fst$FST)
```

```{r}
# Plot Fst vs FstNoCorr
plot(my_fst$FST, my_fst$FSTNoCorr)
abline(0,1)
```

### We need to give OUTFlank a set of quasi-independent SNPs to estimate the neutral FST distribution.

```{r}
# Load additional packages
library("dplyr")
library("stringr")
```

```{r}
# Chromosomes need to be of class integer for this to work.
# Visualizing chromosomes
chrom_unique <- unique(chromosome)
print(chrom_unique)
```

```{r}
# Removing "NC_" from the chromosome name so it can be converted to an integer
chrom_new <- chromosome%>%str_replace("NC_","")

# Converting the character string into an integer
chrom1 <- as.integer(chrom_new)
```

```{r}
#chromosome and position need to be sorted for imputation to work.
chrom_sort <- sort(chrom1)
pos_sort <- sort(position)
```

### Note: This filtering program does not allow for missing genotype values.

Using `snp_fastImputeSimple` to impute missing genotypes

```{r}
# Converting the genotype matrix to class FBM.code256
G1 <- add_code256(big_copy(t(G),type="raw"),code=bigsnpr:::CODE_012)

# Imputing missing genotypes
G_missSimple <- snp_fastImputeSimple(G1,method = "mode")
```

```{r}
newpc<-snp_autoSVD(G_missSimple,infos.chr =chrom_sort,infos.pos = pos_sort)
which_pruned <- attr(newpc, which="subset") # Indexes of remaining SNPS after pruning
length(which_pruned)
```

### Run the OutFLANK() function to estimate the parameters on the neutral FST distribution.

```{r}
out_trim <- OutFLANK(my_fst[which_pruned,], NumberOfSamples=80, qthreshold = 0.05, Hmin = 0.1)
str(out_trim)
```

```{r}
# Check the fit and make sure it looks good, especially in the right tail:
OutFLANKResultsPlotter(out_trim, withOutliers = TRUE, NoCorr = TRUE, Hmin = 0.1,binwidth = 0.001, Zoom = FALSE, RightZoomFraction = 0.05, titletext = NULL)
```

```{r}
# Check the p-value histogram
hist(out_trim$results$pvaluesRightTail)
```

```{r}
# Using estimated neutral mean FST and df to calculate P-values for all loci
P1 <- pOutlierFinderChiSqNoCorr(my_fst, Fstbar = out_trim$FSTNoCorrbar, dfInferred = out_trim$dfInferred, qthreshold = 0.05, Hmin=0.1)
```

```{r}
# Identify outliers SNPs
my_out <- P1$OutlierFlag==TRUE
plot(P1$He, P1$FST, pch=19, col=rgb(0,0,0,0.1))
points(P1$He[my_out], P1$FST[my_out], col="blue")
```

```{r}
P1[which(P1$OutlierFlag == TRUE),]

outliers_out <- P1[which(P1$OutlierFlag == TRUE),]
outliers_out
```

```{r}
# This is a bit complicated, but I'm saving the row names (snp numbers) as a column in the dataframe then extracting those values from the table to save to a .txt file 
out_outliers_list1_8pops <- outliers_out
out_outliers_list1_8pops$snps <- row.names(out_outliers_list1_8pops)
out_outliers_8pops <- out_outliers_list1_8pops$snps
```

```{r}
invisible(lapply(out_outliers_8pops, write, "outliers_outflank_8pops.txt", append=TRUE))
```
